lesson.intro: A pronoun is a word that takes the place of a noun, so we do not have to repeat the noun again and again.
points: Possessive words show who owns something: my, your, his, her, its, our, their (+ noun) and [[mine]], [[yours]], [[his]], [[hers]], [[ours]], [[theirs]] (on their own).
Use "he" for a boy or man, "she" for a girl or woman, "it" for an animal or a thing, and "they" for more than one.
Reflexive pronouns end in -self or -selves: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, themselves.

examples.text: Siti has a kitten. [[She]] loves [[it]] very much.

lesson.tip: When you see "___ and I" or "___ and me", cover the other person's name and read the sentence again: "Me went" sounds wrong, so it should be "I went".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: Siti is my sister. ___ is seven years old.
questions.explanation: Siti is a girl, so we use "she".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: Ahmad likes rice. ___ eats it every day.
questions.explanation: Ahmad is a boy, so we use "he".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: The cat is hungry. ___ wants some fish.
questions.explanation: We use "it" for an animal.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: Mei and I are friends. ___ play together.
questions.explanation: "Mei and I" means "we".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: The children are in the field. ___ are playing football.
questions.explanation: "The children" are more than one person, so we use "they".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: Please give the book to ___.
questions.explanation: After a word like "to" we use the object pronoun "me".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: I saw Encik Lim and waved at ___.
questions.explanation: "Him" is the object pronoun for a man.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: My mother is kind. I love ___ very much.
questions.explanation: "Her" is the object pronoun for a woman.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: This is Kumar's bag. It is ___ bag.
questions.explanation: "His" shows that the bag belongs to Kumar.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: We have a new car. ___ car is red.
questions.explanation: "Our" shows that the car belongs to us.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: The dog wagged ___ tail.
questions.explanation: "Its" shows that the tail belongs to the dog. "It's" means "it is".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: Are these pencils ___?
questions.explanation: "Yours" is used on its own, without a noun after it.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: That house is ___. We live there.
questions.explanation: "Ours" is used on its own, without a noun after it.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: The twins lost ___ umbrella.
questions.explanation: "Their" shows ownership. "There" is a place and "they're" means "they are".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: The teacher asked Ravi and ___ to clean the board.
questions.explanation: Cover "Ravi and": "asked me" is correct.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: Nurul and ___ went to the library.
questions.explanation: Cover "Nurul and": "I went" is correct.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: The prize is ___. She won it fairly.
questions.explanation: "Hers" is used on its own to show that something belongs to her.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: Between you and ___, the test was easy.
questions.explanation: After the preposition "between" we use the object pronoun "me".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: They hurt ___ while playing.
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun for "they" is "themselves". "Theirselves" is not a word.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
questions.sentence: I made this birthday card ___.
questions.explanation: "Myself" shows that I did it on my own.

questions.prompt: Which word is a pronoun?
questions.explanation: "She" can take the place of a girl's name.

questions.prompt: Which word can take the place of "the ball"?
questions.explanation: We use "it" for one thing.

questions.prompt: Which word can replace "my brother and I" at the start of a sentence?
questions.explanation: "My brother and I" = "we".

questions.prompt: Which word can replace "the girls"?
questions.explanation: "The girls" are more than one, so we use "they".

questions.prompt: Which word is a possessive pronoun?
questions.explanation: "Mine" shows that something belongs to me.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Both people are doing the action (subject), so we use "he" and "I".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Possessive pronouns like "hers" never have an apostrophe.

questions.prompt: Which word is a reflexive pronoun?
questions.explanation: Reflexive pronouns end in -self or -selves.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: "Its" (no apostrophe) shows ownership.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: Lina is my friend. He is kind.
questions.explanation: "He" should be "She". Lina is a girl.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: Me am eight years old.
questions.explanation: "Me" should be "I". Use "I" when you are the one doing the action.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: The birds built they nest in the tree.
questions.explanation: "they" should be "their". "Their" shows that the nest belongs to the birds.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: Please give the ball to she.
questions.explanation: "she" should be "her". After "to" we use the object pronoun "her".

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: This pencil is your.
questions.explanation: "your" should be "yours". At the end of a sentence, use "yours".

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: Us like to read storybooks.
questions.explanation: "Us" should be "We". Use "we" when we are doing the action.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: My father and me went fishing.
questions.explanation: "me" should be "I". Cover "My father and": "I went fishing".

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: The cat cleaned itself paws.
questions.explanation: "itself" should be "its". "Its" shows that the paws belong to the cat.

questions.explanation: A sentence starts with a capital letter, has a subject and a verb, and ends with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark.
